# React (TypeScript)

Welcome to your fresh **[Robo.js](https://robojs.dev)** project!

Build, deploy, and maintain your **Discord Activities** with ease. With **Robo.js** as your guide, you'll experience a seamless, **[file-based setup](/docs/discord-activities/file-structure)**, an **[integrated database](/docs/robojs/flashcore)**, **[TypeScript support](/docs/robojs/typescript)**, and a **[rich ecosystem](/docs/plugins)**.

_Ready to embark on this adventure?_

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/discord-activities" title="Documentation" description="Getting started with Robo.js" />
  <Card href="https://robojs.dev/discord" title="Discord" description="Robo - Imagine Magic" />
</Cards>

## Getting Started

Create a project with this template, replacing `<project-name>` with your desired name:

```package-install
npx create-robo <project-name> --template discord-activities/react-ts
```

Then navigate into your project directory:

```bash
cd <project-name>
```

Run development mode:

```bash
npm run dev
```

<Callout>
A free Cloudflare tunnel is included for easy testing. You can copy and paste it into activity's **[URL mapping](/docs/discord-activities/proxy#url-mapping)** to test things out.
</Callout>

## App Development

You can find your client-side code in the `/src/app` folder. This is where you can build your web app using React, Vue, or any other front-end framework.

Things are powered by Vite under the hood, so you get the latest ES modules, hot module reloading, and more!

Try editing the `main` file to get started! (`Activity.tsx` if you're using React)

## Authentication

The React template makes it easy to authenticate your activity with Discord. The `<DiscordProvider>` components in `App.tsx` accepts `authenticate` and `scope` props.

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```tsx
    <DiscordContextProvider authenticate scope={['identify', 'guilds']}>
    	<Activity />
    </DiscordContextProvider>
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="JavaScript">
    ```jsx
    <DiscordContextProvider authenticate scope={['identify', 'guilds']}>
    	<Activity />
    </DiscordContextProvider>
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can then get the SDK and other goodies from the `useDiscordSdk` hook!

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/discord-activities/authentication" title="Authentication" description="Customize your user experience." />
</Cards>

## Backend Development

Your server-side code is located in the `/src/api` folder. This is where you can build your API, webhooks, and other fancy server-side features.

This backend is powered by [**@robojs/server**](/docs/plugins/server) - a powerful Robo plugin that creates and manages a Node `http` server for you. If you install Fastify, the server will automatically switch to it for better performance!

Everything Robo is file-based, so you can create new routes by making new files in the `/src/api` directory. The file's name becomes the route's path. For example, let's try making a new route at `/health` by creating a new file named `health.js`:

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```ts title="src/api/health.ts"
    export default () => {
    	return { status: 'ok' }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="JavaScript">
    ```js title="src/api/health.js"
    export default () => {
    	return { status: 'ok' }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/plugins/server" title="@robojs/server" description="Create and manage web pages, APIs, and more." />
</Cards>

## Folder Structure

While the `api` and `app` folders are reserved for your server and client-side code, you are free to create anything else in the `/src` directory!

Folders only become reserved when you install a plugin that uses them. For example, bot functionality uses the `commands` and `events` folders.

<Files>
  <Folder name="src" defaultOpen disabled>
    <Folder name="app" note="Client-side code">
      <File name="Activity.tsx" />
      <File name="App.tsx" />
      <File name="main.tsx" />
    </Folder>
    <Folder name="api" note="Server routes" disabled />
    <Folder name="commands" note="Slash commands" disabled />
    <Folder name="events" note="Event handlers" disabled />
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="config" defaultOpen disabled>
    <File name="vite.mjs" />
  </Folder>
  <File name=".env" />
</Files>

## Robo Ecosystem

By building with **Robo.js**, you gain access to a growing ecosystem of **[plugins](/plugins)**, **[templates](/templates)**, and **[tools](/docs/cli)**. **[Robo Plugins](/docs/plugins)** are special. They can add features with one command.

```bash
npx robo add @robojs/ai @robojs/sync
```

Plugins integrate seamlessly thanks to the **[Robo File Structure](/docs/discord-bots/file-structure)**. What's more, anyone can **[create a plugin](/docs/framework/plugins/create)**.

## Hosting

**Hosting** your project keeps it running 24/7. No need to keep your computer on at all times, or worry about your Internet connection.

You can host on any platform that supports **Node.js**, or run `robo deploy` to host on **[RoboPlay](https://roboplay.dev)** - a hosting platform optimized for **Robo.js**.

```bash
npm run deploy
```
